description: Verify that DUT TCP queues out-of-order segments and emits a cumulative ACK covering all queued data once the SEQ-number gap is filled (RFC 1122 §4.2.2.20 / RFC 793 §3.9)
approach:
[Objective]
When a segment arrives ahead of an earlier segment (SEQ gap), DUT buffers it and acks only what's contiguous (initial ACK = old expected SEQ). When the gap-fill arrives, DUT emits a cumulative ACK covering everything received.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester ⇄ DUT: handshake.
2. Tester → DUT: segment B (later SEQ; out-of-order).
3. DUT → Tester: ACK of expected SEQ (does not advance because gap exists).
4. Tester → DUT: segment A (the gap-filler).
5. Observation: DUT → Tester: cumulative ACK covering A + B.

[Pass condition]
Final cumulative ACK observed after gap fill.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_no_handshake_ack — handshake never completed
• Fail_no_initial_ack — DUT did not ack initial out-of-order data
• Fail_no_final_cumulative_ack — no cumulative ACK after gap fill

verdicts.Pass: DUT cumulative-acked queued OOO data — normal
verdicts.Fail_no_initial_ack: No DUT ACK to initial data segment
verdicts.Fail_no_final_cumulative_ack: DUT did not emit cumulative ACK after gap fill
